video_title: Luka’s MVP Case, KD’s Frustration & The Porzingis Mystery

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's historic start to the season
quotes.excerpt: He's shooting 42% on 13.7 attempts from three. This that's Steph Curry level. Like no exaggeration.
quotes.quote: Luka has gotten off to an incredible start. There's just no two ways about it. He's got splits of 38, 8 and 8. He's shooting 42% on 13.7 attempts from three. This that's Steph Curry level. Like no exaggeration. The only other person that in both volume and accuracy who can compare is literally the greatest shooter of all time. So he's shooting at a pace of the greatest three-point shooter of all time.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' offensive efficiency with Luka Doncic on the floor
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers are 41.6 points per 100 possessions better with him on the floor in terms of the on-off swing.
quotes.quote: Right now, the Lakers are 41.6 points per 100 possessions better with him on the floor in terms of the on-off swing. Plus 22.5 with him on, minus 19.1 with him off. So basically, they are the best team in the league with Luka on the floor and they are the worst team in the league when Luka is off the floor. That is a wild swing right now.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's impact on Spurs' net rating
quotes.excerpt: Right now, the Spurs are plus 19 net rating with Wembanyama on the floor, minus 15 with Luke Cornet out there.
quotes.quote: Right now, the Spurs are plus 19 net rating with Wembanyama on the floor, minus 15 with Luke Cornet out there. It's close. I think Wembanyama is the favorite to be clear. I don't want to offend you, but I think Wembanyama is the favorite and in assuming San Antonio, like San Antonio is probably going to be the one seed, they'll probably win 60 games and if Wembanyama stays healthy, he will likely win the award.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic as a potential MVP candidate
quotes.excerpt: I'm saying I think Luka should win the award assuming these things stick.
quotes.quote: I'm saying I think Luka should win the award assuming these things stick. But I think there's a difference between what will happen and what should happen. I think Wembanyama is the favorite and in assuming San Antonio, like San Antonio is probably going to be the one seed, they'll probably win 60 games and if Wembanyama stays healthy, he will likely win the award.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.excerpt: The Warriors are no longer paying this dude. They're withholding his checks for services not rendered.
quotes.quote: I just wanted to hit on the weirdness that's happening around Kristaps Porzingis and the Golden State Warriors. Our guy Sam Amick at The Athletic reporting that the Warriors are no longer paying this dude. They're withholding his checks for services not rendered. I mean, he's been away from the team. I mean, at first they said he was going to be around the team, then they said he's been away from the team. Now they're saying he's not, you know, they said they had a plan, sorry, just for people that haven't been paying close attention to this Porzingis thing.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Porzingis's health issues and team status
quotes.excerpt: This has been an insane situation and this predates Golden State, this goes back to Boston.
quotes.quote: This has been an insane situation and this predates Golden State, this goes back to Boston, right? Like he's had this health stuff going on for over a couple years now and has had some extended absences away from his respective teams. The thing that came out right before we started was that not only are they not paying him, but Porzingis and the NBPA are not contesting it as of right now. They are not fighting back.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Porzingis's contract status and team option
quotes.excerpt: Most players, even when they know they're washed and should be in retirement, it's like if I'm owed money.
quotes.quote: Most players, even when they know they're washed and should be in retirement, it's like if I'm owed money, I'm just going to do the bare minimum of what's required of me to show up in order to be paid. Like, yeah, I'm a competitor, I want to play, but realistically, I've earned this money. I signed a contract for this money. That he's forfeiting it is just that's crazy. That's that's bizarre. It's unheard of, honestly.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential mental health component to Porzingis's situation
quotes.excerpt: I wonder if there's a potentially like a mental health component to this where where he just wants to be separate.
quotes.quote: I wonder if there's a potentially like a mental health component to this where where he just wants to be separate from because in theory, when you're trying to return, right? Like you would at least you'd want to be around the team, you want to be there for your teammates and stuff. And if he doesn't even want to do that or isn't capable of doing that for whatever reason, and he's forfeiting the money, it feels like there's something larger at play.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.excerpt: KD, man, it just feels like something's always getting on his nerves. Perpetually unhappy with stuff.
quotes.quote: We got Kevin Durant and I do want to preface this by saying I've been on record for years, it just like KD, man, it just feels like something's always getting on his nerves. Perpetually unhappy with stuff. You know, whether it's Steve Kerr and the system in Golden State, whether it's all the stuff that happened with Brooklyn, the Phoenix situation, certain moments and murmurs that we're hearing from Houston, they start the year beautifully.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Durant's defensive and media interactions
quotes.excerpt: I feel like he tries to present himself as someone who pure hooper loves the game.
quotes.quote: My issue with it is I feel like he tries to present himself as someone who pure hooper loves the game, wants to talk about the game, wants to have these honest conversations. And then when he actually gets pressed on something, he immediately reframes the conversation and gets very defensive. And I think we've seen this on X, we've seen this. It's just like he wants to talk about things on his terms and he wants it to be very pro-KD or very in his favor.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: James Dolan's decision-making is undermining the Knicks' success
quotes.excerpt: Dolan undermining has just been looming under all of this
quotes.quote: Ever since they won the title, and even before they won the title, with inviting Donald Trump to MSG and them losing that game, it felt like the Dolan undermining has just been looming under all of this. He continues to make these out-of-touch decisions that are not good for the Knicks. Whatever magic and juju they had last year, it feels like that is starting to dissipate because of his decision-making.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Questioning the political influence of NBA players
quotes.excerpt: I just don't think they have political king-making abilities

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: I have become cynical about the voice of the player and the empowerment of the player. I just don't think they have political king-making abilities. I don't think that's what players have the power to do. LeBron James opening a school in Akron, Ohio, that he himself is going to fund and pay for and ensure the quality of that school is at a certain standard? Yes, players have the connections and the financial might to achieve those certain kinds of localized goals for people in their communities. These are hyper-focused localized goals. I think individual big players can do that kind of stuff.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: Anything outside of that, I don't think the country at large really looks to NBA players or NFL players to be swayed on political issues. LeBron James in 2016 had just delivered a championship to Northeast Ohio. This dude went all in for Hillary Clinton. As popular as LeBron is at the apex of his popularity after that, he did the impossible. Do you know she got smoked in Ohio?

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential backlash over Knicks players' political associations
quotes.excerpt: The meme potential from the interactions would be a fun day on Twitter

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: If they go, the meme potential from the interactions would be a fun day on Twitter. JD Vance with a smug grin on his face, yucking it up with OG. That might piss me off too, now that I'm thinking about it.

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: First, screw it. Screw my whole argument before that.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: Is that an endorsement from the players of Donald Trump or this administration? No. But I still think there's an element of association, especially in contrast with teams not going. I think this would create a subset of people that would feel certain players need to boycott, and there'd be pressure now on the players to not be there to send a certain message. Jalen Brunson clearly seems to be more on the liberal side, and that puts him in a tough spot potentially of does he go and it's part of this championship celebration, or does he take a stand and make a political statement?
